subject: DPA + Order Form: export routing, SCCs & pricing dependency
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@medico.com>, Procurement Team <procure@medico.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA + Order Form: export routing, SCCs & pricing dependency

Emma / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discussion, I wanted to put the outstanding asks in writing so legal/procurement can align before the next redline exchange. Key points below (attached: redline_v1.docx).

Summary of asks from Medico:
- Confirm that Order Form Exhibit A will include onshore hosting for EU PHI workloads (Medico asked for "EU-only onshore routing").
- Insert standard SCCs and signature flow into the DPA (they want an executed SCCs exhibit).
- Procurement noted a potential pricing dependency: if we are required to provide dedicated onshore KMS and guaranteed data residency for EU accounts, there will be a cost uplift they want visibility into.

What we need from Medico to proceed:
1) Confirm whether the hosting requirement is a hard requirement (must have) or a preference (soft).
2) If hard, confirm expected volume (approx % of tokens or requests that must be routed onshore) so we can size the capacity and produce a pricing delta.
3) Any additional subprocessor constraints — we shared our current list but they flagged a few non-starters.

Internal asks / next steps for Redwood:
- Ben: can you run a quick capacity/pricing sketch for an EU-onshore KMS + dedicated GPU pool? I put a rough deadline of EOD Thursday so we can float a number to Medico for procurement planning.
- Laura: please review the attached redline_v1 and highlight any clauses we should keep as negotiation anchors (data localization, liabilities, export controls, and SCCs flow).

Goal: agree on wording for an Order Form exhibit + DPA clauses so our legal teams can exchange clean redlines and move to DocuSign. Medico asked for a target sign-off within 10 business days if we can provide an indicative price.

Attachments: redline_v1.docx (Order Form + DPA draft)

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Head, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@medico.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procure@medico.com>
Cc: Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@medico.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA + Order Form: export routing, SCCs & pricing dependency

Sergio —

Thanks for the clear summary and the draft. Quick answers from our side:
- The EU onshore hosting is a hard requirement for our regulated EU pilot (PHI and special category data). We cannot route PHI outside the EU for that pilot cohort.
- Initial pilot scope: approx 20% of overall requests in Q4 and expected to scale to ~45% if the pilot is successful.
- Subprocessor concerns: we flagged three subprocessors in your Exhibit list — would like confirmation that none process PHI for EU customers.

Procurement asks that you provide an "indicative uplift" for the onshore KMS + guaranteed routing so we can internalize cost; a ballpark range is acceptable for now. We'll share our standard procurement redline later today for your legal to review.

I scheduled a quick sync for Thursday 14:00 UTC to go over the pricing input — if that time doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Best,
Emma Lawson
Head of Procurement — Medico Systems

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@medico.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA + Order Form: export routing, SCCs & pricing dependency

Team —

I reviewed redline_v1.docx and added comments in dpa_redline_legal_v2.docx (attached). High level legal guidance:
- Keep data localization obligations narrow and tied to a defined customer cohort (Order Form Exhibit) so we don't create a broad "global residency" obligation.
- For SCCs: we can include the standard EU SCCs as an exhibit and a signature block; add a fallback that allows us to rely on other lawful transfer mechanisms should SCCs be invalidated (preserves operational continuity).
- Liability cap: push to keep the MSA cap intact; propose a carve-out for proven regulatory fines but limit to an agreed multiple (e.g., 2x) and only for willful breach of export controls.
- Subprocessor list: propose a short declaration in the DPA stating that current subprocessors will not process EU PHI for the pilot cohort; include a 30-day notice requirement for any changes.

I'll highlight the specific clause language in the attached and flag negotiation anchors. Also flagged a cross-reference mismatch between Exhibit A (Order Form) and the DPA scheduling section — must be reconciled before signatures to avoid operational ambiguity.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@medico.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-16T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA + Order Form: export routing, SCCs & pricing dependency

Emma / Sergio / Laura —

Thanks — pricing sketch attached (summary below). I've assumed the following for an EU-onshore offering:
- Dedicated KMS + onshore key escrow for EU pilot cohort.
- Reserve of 1x medium GPU pool scaled for estimated 20% initial usage (burst policy for ramp to 45%).
- Operational overhead: +10% (monitoring/segregation), infra uplift: +18% baseline.

Indicative uplift ranges (ballpark):
- If pilot remains <=25% traffic routed onshore: +15% to list price.
- If scaled to 25-50%: +25% to list price.
- If >50% or requires dedicated single-customer tenancy: pricing to be discussed (likely >+40%).

We can tighten these ranges after a short discovery call measuring peak token throughput and KMS key rotation frequency. Target: provide a refined number by EOD Thursday 2026-09-17 if Medico confirms traffic volumes and gating constraints.

Operational asks for Medico:
1) Confirm whether the pilot cohort requires dedicated GPU tenancy or whether logical partitioning is sufficient.
2) Confirm SLA expectations for EU-PHI requests (p50/p95 latency and RTO for KMS outages).

If we agree on the ranges, we can mark pricing as "indicative" in the Order Form and add a 60-day re-evaluation clause tied to actual usage. That keeps things moving while protecting both sides.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@medico.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-20T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA + Order Form: export routing, SCCs & pricing dependency

Thanks everyone —

This is helpful and gets us closer. Quick confirmations:
- Pilot scope confirmed at ~20% and we expect to hit ~40–45% within 6 months if pilot succeeds.
- Logical partitioning is acceptable for the pilot cohort (no single-tenant GPU required today).
- SLA expectations: p95 latency matched to existing Redwood Standard plan; KMS RTO acceptable per your standard KMS SLA with a 30-minute RTO for critical incidents.

Procurement reviewed Ben's indicative ranges and can accept +15% at pilot launch with a 60-day re-evaluation clause. We will circulate our signed procurement redline (PDF attached) and ask Redwood legal to incorporate Laura's clause language where feasible.

Next step: please send a DocuSign-ready bundle (MSA + Order Form + DPA + SCCs exhibit + Exhibit A with cohort definition) and we'll route internally. Once we have a DocuSign link we can fast-track approvals.

Attachments: medico_procurement_terms.pdf (procurement redline)

Emma Lawson
Head of Procurement — Medico Systems
